## SLogic32U3 – The Logic Analyzer You Wished Existed
## Affiliate program
Share SLogic32U3 and earn rewards. Join our Kickbooster Affiliate Program, spread the word, and earn 10% commission on every backer you refer!
- Getting started is simple:
- ● Sign up for a Kickbooster account
- ● Get and share your unique referral link
- ● Earn 10% commission on every successful referral

Sign up now via Kickbooster!
## 10Gbps Changes Everything.
Stream massive captures directly to your PC's memory — or even SSD. No more buffer limits. No more choosing between depth and speed.
## 1400 MHz. Every Edge Captured.
Up to 1.4 GS/s sampling with 350 MHz digital bandwidth. Catch glitches, runt pulses, and timing violations that slower analyzers miss entirely.
## 32 CH. Coaxial Probes.Signal Integrity Built In.
Every channel ships with coaxial probe cables featuring front-end AFE circuitry at the tip — cleaner signals, less noise, more trustworthy captures at high sample rates.
## Analog Channels, On Demand.
Snap in a $9 ADC module when a job needs analog — twice the sample rate and bandwidth of Logic Pro 16's built-in analog, with range switching and AC coupling it doesn't offer. Don't need it? Don't pay for it.
## Every OS. Every Workflow. Zero Install.
Works with the open-source tools you already know — plus a browser-based host app that needs no installation at all. Plug in, open a tab, start capturing.
Many APPs Support — Pluseview, Ngscopeclient, Web App, ALL-LOGIC, ...
150+ protocol decoders — SPI, I2C, UART, JTAG, SWD, CAN, USB, SDIO, HDMI-CEC, and many more via the Sigrok ecosystem.
## Debug With AI. Not Just Your Eyes.
A built-in MCP server lets AI agents — Claude, Cursor, Codex, and more — trigger captures, decode protocols, and pinpoint failures automatically.
Full MCP protocol support — works with any MCP-compatible AI agent or IDE. Automate regression testing, CI/CD hardware-in-the-loop, and bench debugging.
## Pro Specs. Maker Price.
The logic analyzer you wished existed — at a price you didn't dare wish for.

## About SLogic & Sipeed
SLogic32U3 is the 3rd generation of the SLogic series, following SLogicCombo8 and SLogic16U3.
The series has always been built around one idea: professional instruments should be affordable for the developers who actually use them. That is why we developed our own 10 Gbps FPGA IP in-house — it lets SLogic32U3 deliver professional-grade performance while staying close to the price of the ordinary USB 2.0 logic analyzers already on every bench. For a developer's toolkit, that combination is the best!
Sipeed is a startup working on open-source AI hardware and software. Our work reaches well beyond FPGAs — our RISC-V boards, NanoKVM devices and on-device AI
products have all found a following in the open-source community.
And we have something else on the way: a palm-sized personal AI supercomputer at 1/3 the power and 1/3 the volume of a DGX Spark, but speed surpass it. Stay tuned.

faq.q: Why is SLogic32U3 so much cheaper than comparable analyzers? Is there a catch?
faq.a:
The savings are in the design, not in the parts we left out.

Instead of pairing the FPGA with an expensive USB 3.2 Gen2 PHY chip, we developed ourown IP that drives the 10 Gbps link directly from the FPGA's SerDes. That removes acostly component from the bill of materials and lowers the FPGA resource budget at thesame time. Combine that with Sipeed's supply chain and a deliberately thin margin, andyou get professional-grade specifications at this price.

One thing worth knowing: memory prices a…

faq.q: What is the current list of supported protocols for parsing?
faq.a:
We support a wide range of protocols, too many to list here. Please refer to the supported list in the link below: 
https://sigrok.org/wiki/Protocol_decoders

faq.q: Does my computer support 10 Gbps USB?
faq.a:
Almost certainly. As of 2026 virtually every x86 machine has a 10 Gbps USB port — even entry-level N100 mini PCs do — and so does every Apple Silicon Mac.

The exception is embedded hosts. A Raspberry Pi's USB 3 port runs at 5 Gbps, and
SLogic32U3 negotiates down to 5 Gbps automatically rather than refusing to work. You simply get proportionally less streaming bandwidth.

faq.q: Why is there no buffer mode? How long can a stream capture run?
faq.a:
Because our stream mode is already as fast as other analyzers' buffer mode.

SLogic32U3 streams at 800 MiB/s straight into your PC, which means capture length is set by your computer rather than by a small memory chip on the board: roughly 20 seconds into 16 GB of RAM, or about 22 minutes onto a 1 TB SSD. A conventional buffer-mode analyzer fills its on-board memory in a fraction of a second at full rate and then stops.
Unlimited depth at full speed is the more useful mode, so it is the one we b…

faq.q: Can the included cables handle the 1.4 GS/s sample rate?
faq.a:
Yes. The included cables are coaxial and shielded, with a measured 3 dB bandwidth of 500 MHz. At 1.4 GS/s the useful signal bandwidth is a quarter of the sample rate —350 MHz — so the cable stays comfortably ahead of what the front end needs.

For signals in that range we do recommend the fine-pitch clips, or soldering directly to the test point. At these speeds the connection at the tip becomes the limiting factor long before the cable does.

faq.q: How do I choose probe clips?
faq.a:
Every kit ships with 32 standard clips included, which cover most through-hole and
larger surface-mount work.
The fine-pitch clips are an optional add-on: they grip TSSOP pins directly, which the
standard clips cannot.

faq.q: How accurate is the optional ADC module? Can it replace an oscilloscope?
faq.a:
The ADC module samples at 100 MS/s with 8-bit resolution, and offers AC/DC coupling and switchable 1× / 2× gain.
Between the compact form factor and the 8-bit depth, it is built for seeing an analog
waveform alongside your digital channels — spotting a rail sag or checking a signal
level in the same timebase as the bus transaction that caused it. It is not intended for
precise voltage measurement, and it complements a bench scope rather than replacing one.

faq.q: Does the web app collect data from my circuit?
faq.a:
No. It is a pure front-end application: all processing and all captured data stay on
your own machine, and our server does nothing but serve the page itself.

If you would rather not rely on our site at all, you can download the page file and run
it entirely offline.

faq.q: Is the AI debugging feature a paid add-on?
faq.a:
The MCP server and the SLogic skills are free from us — there is nothing to buy fromSipeed.
Running them consumes tokens from whichever AI assistant you connect, so you will need your own API credit or subscription with that provider. The feature is entirely optional, and SLogic32U3 is fully functional without it.

faq.q: What stage is the project at, and when will it ship?
faq.a:
A first pilot run of 200 units is already complete. The second batch of 1,000 units goes
into production in October, with shipping to backers in November.

updates.title: Update for Backers Who Added the ADC Module
updates.text:
Dear backers, thank you for supporting us from the very beginning of this project.
For the ADC module you added on, after reviewing feedback from some backers and conducting our own internal testing, we have decided to make some updates to this component.
The main goal is to address the risk of breakage caused by repeated bending of the soldered connection wires. The key changes are as follows:
- Reduced the size of the DIP switch used for AC/DC and gain selection.
- Replaced the soldered connection wires with an MMCX connector for easier replacement.
